quotes.text: Disputes for Instant Bank Payments don’t map to the same eight categories as other payment methods. Every dispute for Instant Bank Payments uses the same dispute reason, `debit_not_authorized`, with the underlying ACH return code shown as the network reason code.
The customer claims they didn’t authorize the debit.
A permissible return entry, for corporate (CCD and CTX) accounts only.
For the evidence that helps you respond to each return code, see [Disputed Instant Bank Payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/instant-bank-payments/disputed-payments.md).

findings: New raw 278-292 adds a separate Instant Bank Payments dispute mapping absent between old Cash App Pay 266-278 and old defense guidelines 280: every such dispute uses debit_not_authorized, with the underlying ACH return as network reason code, and seven return rows R10/R07/R08/R11/R29/R05/R31. This is the central material change.

Current source summary at line 13 says all payment method reason codes map into eight categories, and concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md:68 repeats all-payment-method language. These need scoped correction for the new explicit Instant Bank Payments exception; the existing eight-category card/wallet/BNPL mapping and Visa-only noncompliant framework remain useful within their documented scope.

New Mastercard general list adds 4999 Domestic Chargeback Dispute (Europe Region Only) at raw line 107, absent from matched old list. The new Mastercard Noncompliant|None row at 129 makes an already described no-Noncompliant status explicit, not a new category.

The extensive evidence-table diff largely normalizes Markdown table padding/separators and minor prose; the physical/digital/offline evidence fields and category defense structure remain present through new raw EOF. New see-also links at 997-1002 are navigation. No outcome, eligibility, or account behavior is established by the linked Instant Bank Payments page, which was not read as this job's authority.

Current source lines 64 and 66-68 assert Visa CE 3.0 eligibility, mandatory and Stripe-pre-populated customer_name/billing_address/shipping_address/shipping_carrier/shipping_tracking_number, a no-edit rule, and automatic ECI plus 3DS data population. Neither the matched old nor new categories raw documents those CE 3.0-specific requirements or automation. New raw 492-496, matched old 487-491, says a successfully 3DS-authenticated fraudulent payment can be argued for liability shift and Stripe automatically provides ECI; new 506-562, old 501-559, lists generic Compelling Evidence suggestions and field labels by product type. Generic field suggestions are not evidence of CE 3.0 requiredness, eligibility, autofill, edit restrictions, or automatic 3DS data. Coordinator should remove those source claims or verify and re-source them independently during promotion.

The matched old capture moves directly from Cash App Pay to defense guidelines (old raw:266-280), so this exception is new to the capture. The mapped [[source-stripe-disputes-categories]] summary at line 13 overstates the rule as applying to all payment methods.
